chunks: From him, from Jaʿfar ibn Samāʿah, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from al-Ṣabbāḥ ibn Sayābah and Abū Usāmah, who said: They asked the Shaykh about Maghrib, and he said:
Some of them [say]: May Allah make me your ransom, we wait until a star rises.
So he said: [This is] Khattābiyyah. Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام brought it down to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم when the disk had set.

key_terms.الْقُرْصُ: the disk, i.e., the disk of the sun
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib salat (prayer) or its time
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, the angel who conveyed divine instruction
key_terms.خَطَّابِيَّةٌ: the Khattabiyyah, a deviant sect whose view is being rejected
key_terms.سَقَطَ: set or fell, referring here to the setting of the sun’s disk
key_terms.كَوْكَبٌ: a star, mentioned here as a disputed sign for waiting
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ: the Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) begin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) and rejects delaying it until the appearance of a star. The Imam identifies that view with the Khattabiyyah and affirms that Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام conveyed the ruling to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم when the sun’s disk had set.
